seg.<strong>En résumé</strong><br>Meatball P:
In short
Meatball Party 2D is the tension of the Meatball Speedway condensed into a board game that's easy to pick up, unpredictable every game, and commentated like a real race. A roll of the dice, a dilemma, a duel — and again.

seg.<strong>Damien Przybylski</strong> vit u: Damien Przybylski is having a frustrating start to the season. 24th at Darlington in the first race of the truck division, which follows its own calendar, then 36th at Atlanta after an unavoidable crash ahead of him right at the start of the race.
seg.Notre activité principale se déroule dan: Our main activity takes place in the IFRN league, but we're also entered in other leagues, and we regularly race in official iRacing races, both on ovals and in road endurance events.
seg.💡 <strong>Pour les rookies</strong> : le: 💡 For rookies: the biggest points lever is finishing on the lead lap without hitting anyone — it's worth far more than taking a risk to scrape 2-3 places. Finishing clean in a lower division earns a nice spot in the standings.
seg.Le <strong>Meatball MC</strong> est avan: The Meatball MC is above all a team built on training. We set up personalised training and coaching programmes on request, so you can progress at your own pace with real support; helping each other is part of our DNA.
seg.<strong>Une seule règle à respecter :</s: Only one rule: don't distort the logos and don't add anything to them. If you want a colour variant or a specific adaptation, ask directly on our Discord and we'll handle it with you rather than having files tampered with on your side.
seg.<strong>Verdict (totalement impartial)</:

A free turn-based party game, playable on Android, with your teammates as guest stars on the Meatball Speedway? We've seen less deserving GOTYs. The game is waiting for you in the shop; the only queue is for the photo.
seg.<strong>Chicagoland, 17 septembre.</stro: Chicagoland, 17 September. A decent result for the whole team, with Kevin Charles 8th, Claude Charles 9th and Maxime Toffolet 14th. Beyond the numbers, the message is clear: all our rookies already have the level for the Truck Series.
seg.L’équipe officialise l’arrivée d’une nou: The team makes official the arrival of a new recruit in its training programme: Kevin Charles. At just 16, the young driver takes an important step in his budding career by joining a structure dedicated to learning and developing the talents of tomorrow.
seg.<strong>Nicolas Ciappara</strong> confir: Nicolas Ciappara confirms he's as comfortable on a superspeedway as on a track as technical as Darlington. 5th at Daytona, then 6th at Darlington, snatched after a crazy late charge at the very end of the race. Speed, nerve, and already big points on the board.
seg.Le club continue de recruter et de grand: The club keeps recruiting and growing. First stop, the CUP division of the IFRN league, where Nicolas Ciappara and Jérôme Durand have signed to carry the Meatball MC colours. Welcome to both of them; we hope they'll fly the team's colours high in this division.

Nothing to remember, unfortunately, for Maxime Toffolet (23rd, DNF). Caught in the successive collisions around him, Maxime keeps gaining experience at his own expense. A round to forget as quickly as possible to start afresh at the next one.

seg.<strong>Durand et Toffolet au drapeau à:
Durand and Toffolet see the chequered flag
True to the house spirit, Jerome Durand and Maxime Toffolet both reached the finish of a particularly attritional race, in 20th and 18th places respectively. Seeing the chequered flag when nearly a quarter of the field retires is also how a team progresses.

Learning the fundamentals: mastering the racing line, managing the tyres and rigorous work in the garage.

seg.<strong>Comment l'obtenir ?</strong><br>:
How do I get it?
The beta is free and can be picked up directly from the site's shop: add the game to your cart, confirm the cart, and the download is yours. Yes, that's all. No, there's no catch. The game is also available on Android, to carry the Meatball Speedway in your pocket.
seg.<strong>Rookie.</strong> Kevin Charles e: Rookie. Kevin Charles is the series' driving force: 4th in the championship with three podiums in his last four races (read his profile just above). Maxime Toffolet, 8th in the standings, took 8th at The Bullring and 10th at Kern. Claude Charles, 12th, scored his best results at Kern (11th) and at The Bullring and Phoenix (13th).
seg.<strong>Jerome Durand : Une régularité m:
Jerome Durand: methodical consistency
Faced with the track's many traps, Jerome Durand showed remarkable control. With a clean race without the slightest mistake, he crossed the line in 6th. This result rewards his consistency and takes him past the symbolic 100-point mark in the overall standings (101 pts).
seg.<strong>Comment on joue</strong><br>Meat:
How to play
Meatball Party 2D can be played solo against AI drivers, locally with several players around the same screen (hotseat), or online with friends, with a waiting room and built-in text and voice chat so you don't miss any of the atmosphere even from afar. An options panel lets you adjust volumes and display for a tailor-made game, whatever the screen.
seg.<strong>Alexis Joube : Une réaction exem:
Alexis Joube: an exemplary response
After the setback at Pocono, Alexis Joube responded with authority on track. On a tricky circuit he established himself as the best of the chasers, taking a solid 4th place just off the podium dominated by Antoine Higelin. This performance reverses the trend and puts him back in a favourable position in the championship.
seg.<strong>Kevin Charles : Un apprentissage:
Kevin Charles: a formative lesson
In his first outing with the team at 16, young Kevin Charles got a measure of how demanding the field is. Behind the wheel of an unforgiving car, a few rookie mistakes brought his race to an early end (17th, DNF). A demanding but essential experience to strengthen his foundations in the discipline.
seg.<strong>Cup.</strong> Jérôme Durand a en: Cup. Jérôme Durand put together a fine run at Charlotte (7th), Phoenix (8th) and above all Talladega, where he took pole and finished 4th. Yet he just missed out on the Chase, 14th in the standings. Cédric Colleau continues his learning with a best result at Charlotte (12th), while Thomas Daries, 7th at Las Vegas, has been seen less on track in recent weeks.
seg.<strong>Gateway, 15 septembre.</strong>: Gateway, 15 September. Alexis Joube got the job done. Among the fastest of the night and formidable on the long run, he took a deserved podium in 3rd. For his part, Johann Bourgouin finally opened his points account with 20th place, after a start to the season marked by bad luck. A first step that should lead to more.
seg.<strong>Version de test : on pose le cad:
Test version: setting the scene
Let's be clear, and it matters: Meatball Party 2D is a test version. The game is still in full development, and you'll inevitably come across things that creak, rules that change and surprises nobody planned. That's the point of a beta: you play, you break, we fix.
seg.<strong>Thomas Daries : Des points préci:
Thomas Daries: precious points saved
Struggling to find the right pace on this winding layout, Thomas Daries had a gruelling race. Delayed by a long pit stop for repairs, he showed perseverance to take the chequered flag in a well-earned 14th place, collecting points that could prove decisive in the final count.
seg.Le mercato ne s'arrête pas là : plusieur: The transfer window doesn't stop there: several rookies have also joined the club in the IFRN ARCA division (the 4th division), where they'll join Maxime Toffolet, already in place. They are Mark Vandale, Heynderickx Jason and Martinez Pierre André. The club will be there to support them, help them progress and climb the league's ladder.
seg.<strong>Cédric Colleau</strong> a été ma: Cédric Colleau was unlucky at Daytona, handed a meatball for a small knock early in the race. Surely his way of telling us he's happy to be part of the team. He then took 23rd place in a tough Darlington and got his points tally going. No doubt he'll make the most of his almost full licence in the next races, which promise to be eventful.
seg.<strong>Cap sur l'IFRN</strong><br> Le c:
Next stop, IFRN
The summer championship closes its doors, but there's no time to breathe: the team moves straight on this week to the IFRN championship. A Meatball MC team manager sets the tone for this new campaign: “Our philosophy this season will be to finish races before asking ourselves whether we can win. Consistency and good behaviour are expected.”
seg.Petite particularité qui nous définit :: A little quirk that defines us: we've built all this around the theme of a motorcycle club... in cars, yes, we fully own the joke. Every driver starts at the very bottom of the ladder (Hang-Around) and climbs the ranks one by one (Prospect, Member, Sergeant at Arms, First Officer...) with clear goals at each step to progress seriously, but always with a bit of fun in the air.
seg.<strong>C'est quoi, Meatball Party 2D ?<:
What is Meatball Party 2D?
Imagine a Sunday-night board game that grew up beside a NASCAR oval. Developed by Otimpa3D Studio, Meatball Party 2D is a turn-based video board game where you roll the dice, suffer strokes of fate and face dilemma after dilemma on the most legendary track in the history of virtual motorsport: the Meatball Speedway.
seg.<strong>Chapeau les champions</strong><b:
Hats off to the champions
Impossible to close this season without saluting its two great men. Petr Smetana takes the Season #05 title with 296 points, at the end of a relentlessly consistent campaign — an undisputed champion. Behind him, Gwendal Goasmat locks up runner-up (242 pts) with the authority of the greats. Two drivers who fully deserve their ranking: well done to them.
seg.<strong>Nicolas Ciappara : Une remontée:
Nicolas Ciappara: a controlled comeback
The race quickly got complicated for Nicolas Ciappara, who suffered damage in the very first laps. Showing fighting spirit, he managed to haul his damaged car up to 8th place at the finish. Thanks to the joker race system, he limits the points loss perfectly and puts himself ideally in ambush for the overall standings.
seg.<strong>PERSPECTIVES : LA DÉCISION SUR L:
OUTLOOK: THE DECIDER ON THE MICHIGAN OVAL
The team now has three contenders (Alexis Joube, Nicolas Ciappara and Thomas Daries) for the two remaining podium places alongside Smetana. While dislodging Gwendal Goasmat (2nd with 212 pts) will be a major challenge, the tiny 2-point gap to Alexis Joube and Nicolas Ciappara's proximity promise a very close fight.
seg.<strong>Kevin Charles</strong> nous a mo: Kevin Charles showed us an excellent attitude by not overdoing it and being very serious in his preparation. The speed is there; he still lacks calm and experience to get used to the pressure of an oval race. 13th at USA Speedway and 21st at Nashville, which keeps him not far from the promotion zone. He can only improve race after race and will become more and more solid.
seg.🛡️ <strong>Jerome Durand : Courageux au:
🛡️ Jerome Durand: brave to the end of the night
A dark night but a captain's fight for Jerome Durand (19th). Harpooned and heavily damaged in the very first laps by a teammate, Jérôme saw his hopes of big points vanish from the start. Forced to rack up laps down, he never gave up and completed his 74 laps at a pace that was nonetheless very competitive. A real show of character through the pain.
seg.<strong>Les duels</strong><br>Deux voitu:
Duels
Two cars landing on the same space means a guaranteed collision. The game then triggers a duel: the two tokens face off, and each driver's fighting spirit (Fight) and racing sense (Racecraft) decide, by probability, who stays ahead and who drops back a space. The lower score always keeps a chance of getting away with it; on an oval, anything can happen until the chequered flag.
seg.<strong>Comment ça fonctionne ?</strong>: How does it work? The very first ratings were drawn up from the results and debriefs of the first 5 races of the SBG Legends season, race after race, line after line, cross-checking real performances, observed driving style and everyone's feedback. Each driver's iRacing iR was also taken into account, but only lightly, as a starting point, not as an absolute truth.
seg.L'industrie du jeu vidéo retient son sou: The video game industry is holding its breath. While some studios line up nine-figure budgets and CGI trailers, the gaming event of the year comes from right here: Meatball Party 2D, by Otimpa3D Studio, is available right now as a free beta. The riot scenes (illustration photo above, barely exaggerated) speak for themselves.
seg.<strong>Un instant.</strong> Ce que vous: Hold on. What you're about to discover isn't just a site update. It's a new way to experience our season. Today, the Meatball MC officially launches its own "Ultimate Team" style rating system: individual driver cards, with numerical ratings for every facet of driving: pure speed, long run management, wheel-to-wheel combat, concentration, composure and racecraft.
seg.<strong>Ignite.</strong> Etienne Senamau: Ignite. Etienne Senamaud delivered the division's standout result with a superb 2nd place at Charlotte. Christophe Gasse kicked things off with a podium at Gateway (3rd) and two 12th places at Phoenix and New Hampshire. Damien Przybylski, meanwhile, lifted his head in the last two races (16th at New Hampshire, 18th at Homestead) after a difficult spell. None of our truckers is in the Chase, but they all still have races to finish the season in style.
seg.<strong>Arnaud Dehu</strong>, c'est la r: Arnaud Dehu is the revelation of this start of the season among the rookies. Fast, consistent, he has shown he can handle pressure and has a real skill for criss-cross overtakes, his speciality. 4th at USA Speedway and 6th at Nashville, where all he lacked was a proper long run. Above all, he showed a wisdom few rookies have, choosing to secure the points rather than take risks to chase the top 3. Well done!
seg.<strong>MulotTV et Capmatt43 commentent:
MulotTV and Capmatt43 commentate everything
No way to play in silence: MulotTV and Capmatt43 follow the race live from their booth and react to every Dilemma, every duel, every twist, with more than 250 different lines. Between running punchlines and their double act, they turn every turn of the game into a show, right up to the famous meatball flag (the black flag with an orange disc that signals a mechanical issue and a forced return to the pits).
seg.💥 <strong>Alexis Joube : La grosse décep:
💥 Alexis Joube: the big disappointment of the night
Under the spotlight after a superb qualifying session that put him 2nd on the grid, Alexis Joube (29th, DNF) lived a real nightmare. He missed his gear at the start, panicked, then downshifted by accident. Result: engine blown on the spot on the line and a massive pile-up behind him. In future he'll absolutely have to keep his hand away from the paddles to avoid such mistakes!
seg.<strong>Alexis Joube : le rêve brisé tro:
Alexis Joube: the dream shattered too soon
Two points off 2nd place before this final, Alexis Joube had legitimate ambitions. They vanished in the first laps: a collision with an opponent brought his race to an early end (retirement), preventing him from fighting the battle he had prepared for runner-up. Frustrating, of course, but his final 5th place (221 pts) reflects a solid season that firmly places him among the strong men of the field.
seg.<strong>Bristol, 22 septembre.</strong>: Bristol, 22 September. Another podium for Alexis Joube, 2nd, with the feeling there was much more to be had. Above the rest in pace and speed, he had to shake off stand-ins with avoidable aggression, which cost him a win that was there for the taking. Two podiums in two races: the race for promotion is on more than ever. Johann Bourgouin, for his part, put in a clean race despite a lack of speed and a crash ahead of him, 26th at the finish.
seg.⚠️ <strong>Nicolas Ciappara : Le podium:
⚠️ Nicolas Ciappara: the podium slips away in the last run
For Nicolas Ciappara, the script was cruel. After a solid and very smart start to the race, avoiding the many yellow flag traps, everything was going to plan. The podium was there for the taking... until a driving error in the final run damaged his right wheel. Unbalanced, Nicolas had to fight his car at the end to limit the damage and hang on to 7th. A frustrating end given his early pace.
seg.<strong>Thomas Daries</strong> a lancé s: Thomas Daries launched his season with his trademark rigour. 11th at Daytona to secure the points in the opener, then a very strong showing at Darlington where he took a thoroughly deserved 3rd place, as solid on the long run as in the final sprint. And as if that wasn't enough, he cruised to victory in the truck race at Atlanta, with racing intelligence far above the competition: a set of tyres saved early in the race, then a commanding finish. The boss showed the way.
seg.<strong>Nicolas Ciappara : si près du bu:
Nicolas Ciappara: so close to the goal
Nicolas Ciappara gave everything to the very end. With a fine race, in the right group for almost the whole event, he had the championship podium within reach. But the Michigan oval forgives nothing: an accident in the very last moments of the race dropped him to 14th, shattering his hopes. He ends the season just off the podium, 4th with 227 points, two small points behind his teammate. A cruel conclusion that shouldn't overshadow a very high-level campaign.
seg.<strong>Gateway, 16 septembre.</strong>: Gateway, 16 September. A night to forget for many of our drivers. Thomas Daries took damage before the start even happened, a handicap he dragged around all race without ever being able to show his true level: 16th at the finish. Nicolas Ciappara was also hit early on and wisely secured the points with 14th place. For Jérôme Durand, the race ended before it had even begun: out on the first lap when he had the pace to fight for the top 5, he finished 30th.
seg.<strong>Bristol, 23 septembre.</strong>: Bristol, 23 September. Thomas Daries set the record straight with a fine race ending in 7th place. Cédric Colleau confirmed his good form with a clean race at the pace of the pack, 14th at the finish. Nicolas Ciappara, who never seemed comfortable on the legendary Tennessee oval, did what was needed by securing the points in 15th. As for Jérôme Durand, fast once again, he was caught in yet another crash that wasn't his doing (29th). His luck is bound to turn.
seg.🌟 <strong>Thomas Daries : Une prestation:
🌟 Thomas Daries: an XXL performance, 0.02s from victory!
With an almost perfect race from first lap to last, Thomas Daries was the big man of this round. Sharp, consistent and commanding in every sector of the track, he fought like a lion against leader Petr Smetana. Thomas crossed the line in 2nd, missing out by a whisker, just 22 thousandths of a second! A major performance that makes its mark and puts him very firmly on the provisional championship podium (3rd with 193 points).
seg.<strong>Thomas Daries : la course qu'il:
Thomas Daries: the race he had to run
In a final where the slightest excess could cost a whole season, Thomas Daries delivered exactly the race the situation demanded. Constantly at the front, he crossed the line in 5th, less than a second behind the winner, without ever putting his points haul at risk. A management of exemplary maturity that secures him 3rd in the championship (229 pts) and gives the team a deserved podium after a remarkably consistent season. The result of thorough work, rewarded on the finest stage.
seg.<strong>Bristol, 21 septembre.</strong>: Bristol, 21 September. Back as a stand-in for Alexis Joube, and this time the strategy was right. Perfect tyre management, the same pace as the best with a hundred more laps on the tyres, a pit stop at the ideal moment then an aggressive, controlled finish: victory was the reward, and it was crystal clear. Christophe Gasse finally opened his points account with 15th place, having managed to secure it despite damage in the chaos of the Bristol pack. A tougher night for Damien Przybylski (33rd), on a track that forgives nothing.
seg.<strong>Un mot important avant que ça pa: An important word before things go in all directions: as in FIFA, a player is sometimes rated badly compared with their real level at the start of the season: a profile that takes time to emerge, data that's still too thin, a style that doesn't quite fit the boxes yet. That's normal, and nobody should take it personally. It's only the beginning. These ratings will be refined race after race, and if we see that a driver is clearly underrated (or overrated) compared with what they show on track, the rating algorithm will be adjusted accordingly. Nothing is set in stone.
seg.<strong>Kansas, 24 septembre.</strong> E: Kansas, 24 September. And what a night! Maxime Toffolet delivered a race of excellent control, smart, building up his pace and carefully avoiding the crashes, to take a superb 2nd place. The progress since the disqualification in the first round is impressive. Claude Charles was exemplary: he has already understood how to behave to score points when you have a bit less speed than others, and he was rewarded with a very fine 7th place. Kevin Charles, finally, secured 8th. Three drivers in the top 8, an excellent overall result that does credit to the Meatball MC's seriousness.
seg.<strong>Chicagoland, 14 septembre.</stro: Chicagoland, 14 September. A huge, huge performance from Etienne Senamaud. Fast and flawless on track from start to finish, he took a superb 2nd place that wipes away the poor start to the season in one go. Well done! Stepping in as stand-ins, Alexis Joube and Nicolas Ciappara had the pace to fight at the front but were caught out by a poor tyre strategy, which forced them to run a whole stint on worn tyres. They still finished 6th and 7th after a fine comeback. Damien Przybylski managed to score points (17th), while Christophe Gasse unfortunately suffered avoidable damage early in the race once again (33rd).
seg.<strong>Maxime Toffolet</strong> a vécu: Maxime Toffolet had an infuriating first round at USA International Speedway. Pushed around by competitors who were a bit too aggressive, he ended up exceeding the race's X limit and was disqualified. An 18th place that is still a good result for a bad race. The reaction came at Nashville, even though he played with fire by going through the last-chance race to reach the main event. The progress compared with the first round is huge: he showed he could climb through a pack that gave him no gifts. Not perfect, a few small imperfections, and once again on the edge of disqualification, but he didn't flinch. A fine 10th place rewards his exemplary attitude at the end of the race.
seg.<strong>Le concept</strong><br>Chaque jo:
The concept
Each player takes on a driver and tries to finish the race in front, with rolls of the dice. But there's no real straight line in this game: between two rolls, the track throws Dilemmas at you. Mechanical failure, an accident ahead, a yellow flag in the pits, threatening rain, an unshakeable opponent in your mirror... each time, you have three choices: Safety (take no risk, limit the damage), Risk (all or nothing, glory or the wall), or Tactics (bet on your driver's qualities — Speed, Racecraft, Concentration, Composure, Race management, Fight... — to get out of it with your head rather than your guts). Twelve spaces on the board, split into six categories (mechanical, accident, pits, overtaking, traffic management, race steward), can trigger a Dilemma, and with them, never the same race twice.

txt.Depuis la victoire en truck à Bristol, l: Since the truck win at Bristol, the Meatball MC hasn't been idle. Two IFRN wins, successes in other leagues, two drivers qualified for the Chase and fine international recognition: it was time to take stock. A look back at six weeks of racing.

This time it's a different track, a different car and a different context. My goal will simply be to complete the 45 laps.”
txt.« On te souhaite de très belles vacances: “Have a wonderful holiday, dear Johann! We hope your deep-sea dive goes perfectly, far from the noise of engines and yellow flags. Recharge your batteries at the bottom of the ocean and come back to the surface in top shape for the battles ahead!”
txt.Le steering ratio dans iRacing (surtout: Steering ratio in iRacing (especially in NASCAR) controls the sensitivity and "speed" of the steering. It doesn't affect the car's mechanical behaviour (grip, balance...), only the feel and how much you turn the wheel to get a given steering angle.
txt.« Kevin a la fougue de son âge et une vr: “Kevin has the fire of his age and a real desire to succeed, which is excellent raw material,” stresses the head of the young drivers programme. “But the elite is a world apart. Our role is to stop him skipping steps. Before dreaming of the top, you have to master every step.”
txt.Ratio bas (8:1 ou 10:1) → direction rapi: Low ratio (8:1 or 10:1) → fast, reactive, more direct steering. High ratio (12:1, 14:1, 16:1) → softer steering, more progressive corrections. Advantages of a high ratio: smoother steering, less punishing on mistakes, better feel on long runs where tyre management is key.
txt.Deux manches déjà au compteur pour la no: Two rounds already done in the new IFRN season, and the Meatball MC is fighting on every front: Cup, Access, Trucks and Rookies. Between moments of brilliance, strokes of bad luck and close calls, this start of the campaign already outlines an ambitious roster. A round-up, division by division.
txt.De son côté, Nicolas Ciappara (5e avec 1: Nicolas Ciappara (5th with 145 pts), meanwhile, should logically close the gap to the top: with one race fewer than his direct rivals, the joker rule (dropping the worst result at the end of the season) will cancel out that absence and give him his full weight in the race for the podium.
txt.Kevin se présente volontiers comme le cr: Kevin readily presents himself as the prodigy of his generation. What is that based on, when he hasn't won yet? The answer has the merit of honesty. “On nothing at all. I believe in it 100%, simply because I know that if it doesn't work, I'll do everything to make it work, even if it takes me five years.”
txt.Au classement général, la bataille fait: In the overall standings, the battle is raging with only 3 races left on the calendar. With Petr Smetana (221 pts) and Gwendal Goasmat (212 pts) firmly established at the top, the title looks particularly hard to reach for Alexis Joube (3rd with 177 pts) and Thomas Daries (4th with 158 pts).
txt.Quelle manche sous haute tension ce jeud: What a high-tension round this Thursday! Between a fight for the win decided by a thousandth of a second, strokes of bad luck, avoidable mistakes and a series of collisions, this Round 6 at Pocono gave our drivers an emotional rollercoaster. A full look back at the key moments of the race.
txt.Deux semaines de course, de Chicagoland: Two weeks of racing, from Chicagoland to Kansas via Gateway and the Bristol arena, and a Meatball MC that alternated moments of brilliance and hard knocks. One win, three podiums, rookies maturing before our eyes and a Cup division that mostly learned to take the hits. A round-up, division by division.
txt.Hors IFRN, Alexis a aussi fait parler la: Outside IFRN, Alexis also let rip. He won the WCNL test race at Phoenix, the new league launched by Nicolas Ciappara which will start soon. He also won in Gen 4 Grand National in the HRL league, where he also leads the ARCA championship. A fine haul that confirms his current form.
txt.Une victoire en truck, trois podiums, un: A truck win, three podiums, a rookie division gaining depth and truckers lifting their heads: the momentum is good. The Cup division mostly had bad luck over these two weeks, but the foundations are there. The season is still long, and the Meatball MC has shown it knows how to bounce back.
txt.Actuellement confronté à des catégories: Currently facing categories with still very accessible fields, Kevin isn't short of nerve. The young man already shows overflowing ambition, openly targeting the top and a future win in the First Division. Refreshing enthusiasm, but one that needs channelling in the face of top-level reality.
txt.Début septembre, Kevin était rapide mais: In early September, Kevin was fast but messy: 13th at USA International Speedway, then a dark night at Nashville with 22 incidents. Since October, he hasn't left the top of the table: 4th at Phoenix, 2nd at Oxford Plains, 3rd and a first pole at Kern, then 2nd again at Motegi. He pinpoints the change very precisely.
txt.Prioriser le son des pneus est l'un des: Prioritising tyre sound is one of the best tricks to improve in iRacing, especially in NASCAR. Goal: clearly hear the tyres sliding before the engine sound, to feel when you lose grip or overheat the tyres. So you lower the engine volume to prioritise tyre sound.
txt.Le chiffre des incidents, passé de 22 à: The incident count, down from 22 at Nashville to just 2 at Motegi, tells the same story. “I simply learned to use my brain, and above all I gained experience. I now know all my opponents, so it's naturally easier to anticipate their moves and defend accordingly without putting myself in the wall.”
txt.Alexis Joube, lui, a payé un trafic diff: Alexis Joube, for his part, paid the price of traffic that was hard to manage during the race: stuck behind slower competitors, he could never get back to the front even though he was lapping at exactly the same pace as Goasmat and Smetana. A slightly frustrating P5 given the potential shown, but still a very good result on paper.
txt.Alors posons la question qui fâche : y a: So let's ask the awkward question: could there be a problem with our truckers' preparation? Three drivers, six races, and every time the wrong train at the wrong moment. No need to be defeatist, the season is long and the level is there, that's undeniable. But the momentum is really bad, and it will have to be broken quickly.
txt.Grosse déception à Talladega pour le Mea: Big disappointment at Talladega for the Meatball MC in SBG Legends, the league where the club is flying its colours this season: no luck at all on the superspeedway for our colours this week. Next stop Charlotte next week, with a clear motto: no more room for error if the team wants to stay in the title race.
txt.Pas le temps de souffler, le programme d: No time to catch our breath, the schedule for the next round is already known. The trucks head to Chicagoland, which looks set to be a tense mini superspeedway. Access heads to Gateway, a promising braking track, and the Cup division will be there too. As for the rookies, they'll also head to Chicagoland, like the trucks.
txt.Celui qui commente volontiers les course: The man who readily comments on other people's races also acknowledges the limits of his view. “Ignite, I can judge a little, because I've already done a test race there and faced some of its drivers. For Access and Cup, I have no idea yet. I fully intend to do a test race in Cup if possible, and we'll see how it goes.”
txt.En Access, Alexis Joube a alterné le trè: In Access, Alexis Joube alternated between the very good and the frustrating: 5th at Las Vegas and Phoenix, but a night to forget at Charlotte (35th) and quieter results at Talladega and New Hampshire. The foundations laid at the start of the season were enough: he is qualified for the Chase and sits 2nd, just 15 points behind leader Lucas Montrésor. The title is within reach.
txt.Ça force ton épaule droite à rester plus: It forces your right shoulder to stay higher or tense → fatigue and shoulder/neck pain in the long run. With a positive steering offset (e.g. +10 to +20), you recentre the wheel: both hands stay in a natural, symmetrical position on the straights. Result: less shoulder tension, better endurance on long runs, and you're more relaxed.
txt.Thomas Daries repart avec une voiture ab: Thomas Daries came away with a damaged car after a 3-wide badly handled by a competitor, in a fight started by Alexis but for which he was in no way responsible. Despite the damage, Thomas brought the car home in P8. Johann Bourgouin, true to his method, once again played the submarine far from the fighting to put in a superb race and finish P9.
txt.« Ce qui m'a changé, c'est que j'ai arrê: “What changed me is that I stopped believing I was the best and started again on the right footing. At first it was hard not to think about winning, and in the end it was slowing me down. The real turning point was Kansas. I understood that if I wanted to win, it wasn't up to others to do the work for me, but up to me to learn and create my own luck.”
txt.Alexis Joube ne laisse plus rien passer: Alexis Joube lets nothing slip any more on the legendary Indianapolis oval. Starting 3rd on the grid, the club's Right Hand took control to win after a clean race without the slightest blemish, ahead of a Chris Hargroves more used to contact than fair play, and a combative Attila Joó, both reduced to watching the number 00 pull away towards the chequered flag.
txt.Quatrième du championnat Rookie IFRN, pr: Fourth in the IFRN Rookie championship, first in the Meatball MC Power Ranking, three podiums in his last four races: at 16, Kevin Charles is the team's man in form. He talks a lot, he doubts nothing, and he owns everything. Before heading out at Summit Point, he agreed to answer all our questions, including the spikiest ones. An interview with a driver in a hurry.
txt.En Cup, sa division de cœur, il reste l': In Cup, his favourite division, he remains one of the most consistent drivers in the field: 2nd at Kansas, 5th at Las Vegas, 9th at Charlotte, 7th at Phoenix and 8th at New Hampshire. Only Talladega (29th) spoiled the run. Result: Nicolas is qualified for the Chase, 6th and 34 points behind the leader. Add a 4th place as a truck stand-in at Charlotte, and you get a particularly full autumn.
txt.Au classement, Alexis Joube reste le mie: In the standings, Alexis Joube remains the best placed of the club's colours, with Thomas Daries not far behind, lying in wait. Ahead of them, Czech driver Petr Smetana is running away at the top, chased by a certain Gwendal Goasmat, a newcomer who already looks every bit like a future GOAT of the discipline. Overall, then, Smetana leads, Goasmat lurks, then Alexis 3rd and Thomas 4th.
txt.Nouvelle manche du championnat SBG Legen: Another round of the SBG Legends championship this weekend, and once again the club put drivers in the leading pack. Goasmat and Smetana once more stood above the rest, untouchable ahead of everyone, but right behind them was an in-form Nicolas Ciappara, who finished the race P4 and confirmed he is clearly part of the leading group this season.
txt.Avec 73 points de retard sur l'intouchab: 73 points behind the untouchable Kostek Solowiej, a six-time winner, Kevin isn't kidding himself. “The title is impossible, barring a miracle. But I'm still in the running for runner-up, and the same goes for the team standings, even if that's harder. Anyway, the goal at the start of the season was a top 5 in the championship and a win. My expectations haven't changed.”
txt.Chez les Charles, la course se vit à deu: In the Charles household, racing is a two-man affair. His father Claude also races in the Rookie championship, where he sits 12th with a patient, points-oriented approach. Who advises whom? “It's more me who advises him. I've always been the fastest, even in real life now that I've grown up. But he's anything but slow: if he really wanted to, he'd be even faster. In short, I take after him.”
txt.Dans un setup fixed, seuls 3 réglages so: In a fixed setup, only 3 settings can be changed: steering offset, steering ratio and brake bias — the same principle on every NASCAR car. On the Next Gen, there's no steering box any more, so no classic ratio: instead you adjust the pinion gear size on the steering column, measured in mm/rev (e.g. 40, 60, 80). The higher the mm/rev, the faster the steering — the opposite of the old ratios.
txt.Kevin avait évoqué la création de sa pro: Kevin had mentioned creating his own league. The project is off the table. “I'm thinking about something else with Liam, something that would look like multiclass. For now we're just at the ideas stage.” Putting the cart before the horse, with a dozen IFRN races under his belt? “Exactly, that's why I'm backing off.” A sign of perspective that says a lot about how far he has come in two months.
txt.Il suffit parfois d'une seule escapade h: Sometimes a single trip away from the ovals is enough to remind you how much you love oval racing. For this Round 7, the SBG field tackled an extremely demanding road course behind the wheel of a particularly hard-to-tame machine. Between the many retirements and critical grip management, this round completely reopened the championship ahead of the final showdown.
txt.Comment faire : mesure la distance entre: How to do it: measure the distance between your eyes and the centre of the screen (in cm), use an online calculator (ocracing.com/fov-calculator, dinex86.github.io/FOV-Calculator, simracingcockpit.gg/fov-calculator), enter the screen size, distance and type (single/triple), then apply the Horizontal FOV (hFOV) shown in your game. Tip: set it to your real geometry, not "by eye". The closer you are to the screen, the wider the FOV must be.
txt.Il fallait bien l'ovale rapide de Michig: It took the fast Michigan oval to conclude this Season #05 of the SBG Legends Series. On Thursday 20 August, on the Brooklyn track, 117 high-speed laps settled the final stakes of a championship whose champion was already known, but whose places of honour were still up for grabs. For the Meatball team, this final round looked decisive: two podium steps to go and get, three drivers able to claim them.
txt.Venu prêter main forte en Access, Nicola: Brought in to lend a hand in Access, Nicolas Ciappara struck twice. First at Charlotte on 13 October, where he won after starting 3rd and celebrated with a burnout on the finish line. Then at New Hampshire on 3 November, with a win built from 30th on the grid: a boss-like comeback, with only 2 incidents on the counter. In between, he also took 4th at Phoenix and 6th at Talladega in the same series.
txt.Premier du Power Ranking interne, devant: First in the internal Power Ranking, ahead of all the Cup and Access drivers, he draws no hasty conclusions. “I'm on the second-best run among the Rookies right now, but there's also the slight dip of the Cup and Access drivers that let me take the lead.” And to the veterans waiting for him to slip up, he simply replies: “You'll have to give me a bit more time, but I'll work to grab a win in the near future.”
txt.Les rumeurs de transfert, venues de son: Transfer rumours, coming from his own entourage, got the paddock talking. Kevin confirms them, then closes the subject straight away. “For me it's already very clear: I'll be with the Meatball MC next season at least, and if all goes well, I'll carry on with them. As for teams, three showed interest in me: the Optimates, who tested the waters, SBG Motorhead, who tried implicitly and whom I politely turned down for the second time since I arrived, and Meatball Racing.”
txt.Côté débutants, Jérôme Durand disputait: Among the newcomers, Jérôme Durand was racing his first official race in the club's colours and did rather well despite a strategy call that went wrong: he pitted, a yellow flag came out just after his stop, leaving him a lap down in a championship where wave-arounds are not enabled. Caught out by the timing, he still finished P12. Maxime Toffolet, for his part, was making his debut with the club and delivered a promising race ahead of the upcoming IFRN ARCA season, with an encouraging P11 for a first try.
txt.Son ingénieur de course le décrit comme: His race engineer describes him as a driver who gets angry quickly and sometimes looks for someone else to blame. Kevin doesn't dodge it. “I used to get angry quickly, but Kansas calmed things down. Yes, sometimes I can blame others in the moment, then realise afterwards that the mistake was mine, like with Fred Desautez at Kern.” As for the setbacks that make him lose his cool, he has his method: “Only experience and the reality of racing can train you for that. I just try to calm down and get back into the race.”
txt.Sur le plan comptable, cette épreuve rou: In terms of points, this road course round upsets the hierarchy and clarifies the stakes before the final showdown. With 261 points on the counter, Petr Smetana is now mathematically untouchable and guaranteed to win the Season #05 title. Behind the champion, tension is at its peak: Gwendal Goasmat keeps 2nd place with 212 points, but is under direct threat from Alexis Joube (3rd with 210 points), who has closed to just two points thanks to his fine performance. Lying in wait, Nicolas Ciappara takes advantage of his joker race to move up to 4th with 204 points, within striking distance of the podium, while Thomas Daries (5th with 197 points) remains mathematically in contention. The team thus places three contenders in the top 5 to fight for the two remaining places of honour, promising an explosive finale on the Michigan speedway.
